title: Creating Blue Oceans
coreMove: Shift the strategic question from how to beat rivals to what value leap could make the old comparison less relevant.
sourcePressure: Establish the red-ocean versus blue-ocean contrast, the strategic move as the unit of analysis, and value innovation as the way to create new demand rather than fight over shrinking profit pools.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating blue ocean strategy as a slogan for being creative, disruptive, or nicer than competitors.

sourceAnchors.name: 150 strategic moves across more than 100 years and 30 industries
sourceAnchors.detail: the official book page frames the argument as a study of 150 strategic moves spanning more than a century and 30 industries
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The pattern is not a pep talk about originality; it comes from looking at 150 strategic moves across more than a century of industries.

sourceAnchors.name: Cirque du Soleil
sourceAnchors.detail: the official FAQ lists Cirque du Soleil as a blue-ocean example not driven mainly by new technology
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Cirque du Soleil matters because it changed the value mix of circus and theater, not because it owned a secret technology.

sourceAnchors.name: Canon copier buyer-group shift
sourceAnchors.detail: the official Canon example supports a move from office purchasing managers toward office users in the copier market
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Canon found leverage by asking who actually used the machine, not only who signed the purchase order.

hook: Do not open with a competitor scoreboard, a war metaphor, or a generic market map.
Do not use A crowded market is not..., The real strategy is..., or What if growth... as reusable shells.
counterintuition: Avoid Most people assume... but actually... and The opposite is true.
Avoid turning every chapter into competition bad, creativity good.
tryThisNow: Avoid Set a timer for 60 seconds and list... as a repeated action.
Avoid generic reflect on your strategy prompts.
examples: Avoid conference-room whiteboard workshops as the default scene.
Avoid repeating mugs, markers, dosing cups, bike helmets, radiators, bus depots, classrooms, narrow kitchens, or generic dashboard scenes.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: coffee shop access for parents with strollers
exampleSpecs.audience: a cafe owner losing families to a larger rival across the street
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the next spend goes to a faster espresso machine or a doorway-and-seating redesign that opens demand
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she watches a stroller wedge in the doorway, then crosses out rival speed and marks access, table spacing, and one-handed ordering as the neglected value factors
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A stroller jammed between a brass door handle and a pastry case

exampleSpecs.domain: late-night print rescue between cheap chains and design studios
exampleSpecs.audience: a copy-shop operator facing chain-store price pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether students and small firms see him as expensive or as the only safe rescue after hours
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a student asks for a thesis repair after closing and he must decide whether the market is copying pages or saving deadlines
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Are you still open?" from a student holding a torn thesis binding

exampleSpecs.domain: grocery dinner bundles for exhausted commuters
exampleSpecs.audience: an independent grocer beside a polished chain
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether shoppers keep treating the store as smaller and pricier or as the easiest route to dinner
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the smell of rotisserie chicken and the sight of a half-built basket push her to ask a customer what would make dinner possible tonight
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Steam fogging the plastic lid on an unsold chicken

exampleSpecs.domain: adult beginner swim lessons redesigned around privacy
exampleSpecs.audience: a swim-school director whose lanes are full of children but empty of embarrassed adults
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether adults who cannot swim ever enter the market at all
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he compares the old public-lane schedule with a screened, named-goggles format that treats privacy as core value
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Luca two registration cycles to notice adults never asked twice

exampleSpecs.domain: museum family visits versus unused digital guides
exampleSpecs.audience: a public-programs lead under pressure to raise attendance
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the next budget buys technology or removes the friction that keeps families away
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the tablet launch gets praise but families still leave early, forcing her to separate novelty from a real value leap
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What good is a perfect audio guide if a parent cannot find a quiet place to feed a toddler?

exampleSpecs.domain: bike shop serving nervous first-time commuters
exampleSpecs.audience: a mechanic whose shop is built for enthusiasts
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether he keeps selling performance upgrades or opens demand among people afraid of riding to work
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he predicts speed parts will drive growth, then a first-timer chooses route confidence, tire lessons, and theft help instead
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 6:40 p.m., Daniel lines up three carbon stems under the service light

skillTargets: distinguish blue-ocean value innovation from rivalry, novelty, or technology-first moves
spot excluded demand in a concrete operating scene
choose a value-leap move over feature copying

tryThisNowSpec: Write down the competitor you most want to beat, then list one buyer frustration that competitor comparisons never mention.
